description: The six evaluating agents (docs/02 §3), one service each under services/, all built from the same skeleton by injecting an agent-specific scorer + policy into the libs/acip-agent-common runner/graph from FEAT-001. Each is an ASYNC Kafka consumer: consume txn.evaluate.requested from TXN_EVALUATE, read its slice of the SHARED REPRESENTATION (the orchestrator already built the features - agents do NOT rebuild), compute the numeric signal, get an LLM rationale via llm-gateway with a TEMPLATED fallback (degraded=true) so it never blocks, assemble a Verdict (docs/02 §4), publish agent.verdict.produced to AGENT_VERDICTS keyed by transaction_id, and commit the offset AFTER publish (docs/02 §6). Each also exposes FastAPI /healthz + /readyz, a non-root python:3.11-slim Dockerfile, Settings config, structured logging + trace_id from the envelope, and pytest unit tests for the scoring/verdict logic with llm-gateway + kafka + ml-scoring mocked. Depends on FEAT-001 (acip-agent-common, new config keys). The six verdicts are keyed by AgentName.value and shaped to drive the EXISTING decision-engine aggregate() branches (verified in services/decision-engine/src/decision_engine/aggregator.py), so real APPROVE/DECLINE/CHALLENGE results instead of decide_partial. This is ONE feature (same change pattern x6), with the per-agent specifics in the steps.
steps: risk-agent (AgentName.RISK): services/risk-agent/{Dockerfile,pyproject.toml,src/risk_agent/{__init__,main,scorer,agent}.py,tests/test_risk.py}. scorer calls ml-scoring-service POST /v1/score with model='risk' and the representation.features ordered by acip_common.features.FEATURE_COLUMNS; score=returned prob; decision_hint banded via Settings.approve_max/challenge_max (<=approve_max APPROVE, <=challenge_max CHALLENGE, else DECLINE); evidence from top_features. Verdict carries model_version from the score response. agent.py injects scorer into the acip_agent_common runner. Deps: acip-common, acip-agent-common, httpx==0.28.1.

fraud-agent (AgentName.FRAUD): services/fraud-agent/... scorer calls ml-scoring-service model='fraud' and ALSO weights graph signals from the representation (graph_signals.ring_size / shared_device_ring_size, velocity_1h) so the ring_member scenario yields a high fraud score. Emit score so that the decision-engine hard veto (fraud.score >= Settings.fraud_block_threshold, default 0.85) fires -> DECLINE for the ring; evidence includes shared_device_ring_size + velocity_1h (docs/02 §4 example). decision_hint DECLINE when score>=threshold else banded.

routing-agent (AgentName.ROUTING, docs/02 §3.1 ROUTE-SCORING): services/routing-agent/... scorer enumerates representation.candidate_routes and scores EACH on predicted success x cost x latency (weights from Settings or sensible defaults, documented in the scorer docstring; normalize cost_bps/p50_latency_ms, handle None), returns the ranked routes + chosen_route (highest). Verdict.decision_hint = ROUTE; put the ranked routes + chosen_route into evidence (one Evidence per route, signal=processor, value=route score) so the decision-engine routing overlay (which ranks candidate_routes by success_rate) has the ranked list; score = chosen route's score. Never a hard veto. For unhealthy_preferred_route this picks a healthy alternate over the degraded processor_pref.

policy-agent (AgentName.POLICY): services/policy-agent/... scorer applies rules from Settings: DENY (decision_hint=DECLINE, score=1.0) when representation.transaction geo / graph home_geo is in Settings.policy_sanctioned_geos (default ['XX']) OR amount > a configured limit; collect violated_rules[] into evidence (signal=rule name). allow -> decision_hint=APPROVE, score=0.0. DENY is a HARD VETO (the decision-engine already treats policy DECLINE as a veto). sanctioned_geo scenario (home_geo 'XX') -> DECLINE.

merchant-agent (AgentName.MERCHANT, advisory soft-constraints): services/merchant-agent/... scorer emits merchant preference adjustments + soft constraints; when amount >= Settings.merchant_high_value_challenge (default 4000.0) emit a 'force_challenge' Evidence (value>=1.0) and/or decision_hint=CHALLENGE so the decision-engine upgrades APPROVE->CHALLENGE (it reads force_challenge evidence or a CHALLENGE merchant hint). Otherwise decision_hint=APPROVE with no constraint. NEVER a hard veto. high_value_midrisk (4800) -> CHALLENGE.

checkout-personalization-agent (AgentName.CHECKOUT_PERSONALIZATION, docs/02 §3.2 ADVISORY): services/checkout-personalization-agent/... scorer ranks payment methods by predicted success from representation.method_history (successes/(successes+failures)), returns recommended_method + confidence; put the recommended method name in Verdict.rationale (the decision-engine reads _recommended_method from personalization.rationale) and the ranking/confidence in evidence. decision_hint=APPROVE, advisory only, NEVER vetoes.

For EVERY agent: main.py builds the acip_agent_common health app via make_health_app(runner) (FastAPI /healthz + /readyz; lifespan starts the consumer loop in a daemon thread consuming TXN_EVALUATE with group '<agent>-agents'); the runner calls llm-gateway for the rationale with the templated fallback (degraded=true) and publishes agent.verdict.produced to AGENT_VERDICTS keyed by transaction_id, committing AFTER publish. Non-root python:3.11-slim Dockerfile copying pyproject.toml+uv.lock+libs/acip-common+libs/acip-agent-common+the service dir, installing via `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --package <name>`, uid 10001, EXPOSE 8000, CMD uvicorn <module>.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000. Each pyproject declares acip-common = { workspace = true } and acip-agent-common = { workspace = true } under [tool.uv.sources], fastapi/uvicorn/httpx pinned.

Workspace wiring (per Phase-2 convention): for each of the six agents REMOVE its dir from root pyproject.toml [tool.uv.workspace].exclude, add it to [tool.uv.sources] as { workspace = true } AND to [dependency-groups].dev; run uv sync so pytest/mypy resolve imports. (graph-projector stays excluded until FEAT-003.)

Tests per agent (tests/test_<agent>.py): with ml-scoring-service + llm-gateway + Kafka mocked/injected, assert (a) the scorer maps a representation slice to the expected (score, decision_hint, evidence) for its scenario, (b) the templated LLM fallback sets degraded=true when llm-gateway errors, (c) the runner publishes agent.verdict.produced keyed by transaction_id and commits AFTER publish (ordering assertion). Keep scorer logic pure and directly unit-testable.
acceptance_criteria: All six agent services exist under services/ as uv workspace members (removed from exclude, in sources + dev), each with a non-root python:3.11-slim Dockerfile and FastAPI GET /healthz + /readyz.

Each agent consumes txn.evaluate.requested from TXN_EVALUATE (group '<agent>-agents'), reads its representation slice without rebuilding features, computes its signal, gets an LLM rationale with a templated degraded=true fallback, publishes agent.verdict.produced to AGENT_VERDICTS keyed by transaction_id, and commits the offset AFTER publish.

The emitted Verdicts drive the existing decision-engine branches: fraud score >= fraud_block_threshold -> DECLINE (ring_member); policy DECLINE on sanctioned geo (sanctioned_geo); merchant force_challenge/CHALLENGE upgrade on high value (high_value_midrisk); routing returns ranked routes + chosen alternate (unhealthy_preferred_route); personalization recommended_method surfaced via rationale; clean_shopper low risk+fraud -> APPROVE.

Thresholds/weights come from Settings (approve_max, challenge_max, fraud_block_threshold, policy_sanctioned_geos, policy_high_value_threshold, merchant_high_value_challenge), never hardcoded; the stack runs with NO cloud creds (templated rationale acceptable).
Per-agent pytest unit tests pass with ml-scoring + llm-gateway + Kafka mocked, including the degraded-fallback test and the publish-then-commit ordering test.
verification: uv run pytest services/risk-agent services/fraud-agent services/routing-agent services/policy-agent services/merchant-agent services/checkout-personalization-agent  (all pass)
uv run mypy libs services  (clean, strict)
findings:
DONE. Full FEAT-002 gate green: uv sync (6 agents resolved as workspace members); uv run pytest for all six agents = 30 passed; ruff check . clean; black --check . clean (96 files); mypy libs services strict clean (91 source files). Full workspace suite (libs + all services) = 117 passed, no regressions. Live Docker smoke was NOT run (Docker not exercised here); substituted an in-process five-scenario integration check driving the six scorers + decision_engine.aggregate() — all five resolved as documented: clean_shopper->APPROVE (route processor_a), ring_member->DECLINE (fraud veto), high_value_midrisk(4800)->CHALLENGE (merchant step-up, NOT policy), sanctioned_geo(home_geo XX)->DECLINE (policy geo veto), unhealthy_preferred_route->APPROVE on healthy alternate (processor_a over degraded processor_pref). The temp check script was removed.

=== AgentName each service emits (keyed by AgentName.value in decision-engine) ===
risk-agent -> AgentName.RISK ('risk'); fraud-agent -> AgentName.FRAUD ('fraud'); routing-agent -> AgentName.ROUTING ('routing'); policy-agent -> AgentName.POLICY ('policy'); merchant-agent -> AgentName.MERCHANT ('merchant'); checkout-personalization-agent -> AgentName.CHECKOUT_PERSONALIZATION ('checkout_personalization').

=== Consumer group ids (EventConsumer default = f'{agent}-agents' on TXN_EVALUATE) ===
risk-agents, fraud-agents, routing-agents, policy-agents, merchant-agents, checkout_personalization-agents. Each publishes EventType.AGENT_VERDICT_PRODUCED to AGENT_VERDICTS keyed by transaction_id and commits AFTER publish (inherited from acip_agent_common.AgentRunner; publish-then-commit ordering asserted per agent).

=== Verdict shapes (what each score_fn emits; drives the EXISTING aggregator branches) ===
- risk: calls ml-scoring POST /v1/score model='risk' with features ordered by acip_common.features.FEATURE_COLUMNS; score=returned prob; decision_hint banded by Settings.approve_max/challenge_max; model_version from the score response; evidence = response top_features (signal=name,value=contribution,weight=1.0). MlScoringClient isolates the HTTP call so build_score_fn(client,settings) is pure.
- fraud: ml-scoring model='fraud' base prob COMBINED with a graph component (gather_fn gather_graph_signals pulls shared_device_ring_size/ring_size + velocity_1h from graph_signals, falling back to features). graph_component(ring,vel) saturates to 1.0 at ring>=5 (RING_SATURATION) plus a bounded velocity bump (weight 0.3); final score=max(ml_prob, graph_component). decision_hint=DECLINE when score>=Settings.fraud_block_threshold (0.85) else banded; evidence=[shared_device_ring_size, velocity_1h]. ring_member (ring=5) -> score 1.0 -> engine fraud hard veto -> DECLINE.
- routing: no ml; score_routes() ranks every representation.candidate_route by weighted blend 0.7*success_rate + 0.15*(1-norm_cost) + 0.15*(1-norm_latency) (cost/latency normalized across the set then inverted; None=neutral 0.5). decision_hint=ROUTE (never a veto); evidence = one row per route in ranked order (signal=processor, value=route score, weight=1.0); verdict score = chosen (top) route's score. Healthy processor_a/_b outrank degraded processor_pref (0.42).
- policy: no ml; evaluate_rules() -> DECLINE score=1.0 (hard veto) when home_geo OR txn_geo in Settings.policy_sanctioned_geos (default ['XX']) OR amount > Settings.policy_amount_hard_cap; evidence = one row per violated rule (signal in {'sanctioned_geo','amount_over_hard_cap'}, value=1.0). Else APPROVE score=0.0, no evidence.
- merchant: no ml; advisory, NEVER DECLINE. amount >= Settings.merchant_high_value_challenge (4000) -> decision_hint=CHALLENGE + a 'force_challenge' Evidence (value=1.0) so the engine upgrades APPROVE->CHALLENGE (signal matches decision_engine.aggregator._FORCE_CHALLENGE_SIGNAL). Else APPROVE, no constraint. score=0.0 (advisory, not a risk score).
- checkout_personalization: no ml; advisory, always APPROVE score=0.0. rank_methods() orders method_history by successes/(successes+failures) (neutral prior 0.5 when no history); recommended = top method carried in Verdict.rationale via the NEW ScoreResult.rationale_override (engine reads personalization.rationale as recommended_method); evidence = one row per method (signal=method, value=success_rate); confidence = top method's success rate.

=== acip-agent-common ADDITIVE change (needed so personalization can set a structured rationale) ===
ScoreResult gained optional field rationale_override: str|None=None. graph.AgentGraphState gained a rationale_override channel; _score_node forwards it; _assemble_verdict_node prefers a non-empty rationale_override over the LLM/templated reason text. Backward-compatible: every other agent leaves it None and keeps the LLM/templated rationale (and degraded flag) unchanged. The personalization agent's recommended method therefore survives an llm-gateway failure while the verdict is still marked degraded=true.

=== acip-common ADDITIVE changes ===
1) SharedRepresentation gained optional home_geo: str|None=None and txn_geo: str|None=None so the policy agent can match a specific sanctioned geo (the feature row only folds the pair into geo_mismatch, which cannot identify 'XX'). representation-service builder now populates home_geo=graph.home_geo and txn_geo=txn_geo (the only Phase-2 file touched; purely additive, defaults None).
2) Settings: REMOVED the now-dead policy_high_value_threshold key and ADDED policy_amount_hard_cap: float (alias POLICY_AMOUNT_HARD_CAP, default 10000.0); .env.example mirrors it (POLICY_HIGH_VALUE_THRESHOLD line replaced). THRESHOLD-SEPARATION DESIGN FIX (approved Option B): a policy DECLINE is a HARD VETO while the merchant high-value rule is a SOFT CHALLENGE; the aggregator checks the policy veto BEFORE the merchant upgrade, so the two controls must not share a threshold. Policy's amount veto now fires only on amount > policy_amount_hard_cap (10000), kept above merchant_high_value_challenge (4000), so the 4800 high_value_midrisk scenario CHALLENGEs (merchant) instead of policy-declining. Rationale is documented in policy_agent/scorer.py module docstring; tests assert amount>cap declines AND 4800 does not policy-decline.

=== Workspace wiring (root pyproject.toml, Phase-2 convention) ===
All six agent dirs REMOVED from [tool.uv.workspace].exclude (only services/graph-projector remains, deferred to FEAT-003); each added to [tool.uv.sources] as {workspace=true} and to [dependency-groups].dev. uv sync installs them; pytest/mypy resolve imports.

=== Per-agent files ===
Each services/<agent>/ has: non-root python:3.11-slim Dockerfile (uid 10001, EXPOSE 8000, uv sync --frozen --no-dev --package <name>, copies pyproject.toml+uv.lock+libs/acip-common+libs/acip-agent-common+the service dir, CMD uvicorn <module>.main:app), pyproject.toml (acip-common + acip-agent-common = {workspace=true}; fastapi==0.115.6, uvicorn[standard]==0.34.0, httpx==0.28.1 pinned), src/<module>/{__init__,main,scorer,agent}.py (main.py = make_health_app(build_runner(get_settings())); agent.py injects the scorer into AgentRunner; scorer.py holds the pure, unit-tested logic), and tests/test_<agent>.py (ml-scoring + llm-gateway + Kafka mocked/injected; each suite asserts the scorer maps its scenario slice to the expected (score,hint,evidence), the templated LLM fallback -> degraded=true, and the run_once publish-then-commit ordering). Test module names are unique and test dirs carry no __init__.py (matches the existing service convention).
